analysis.investment_thesis: Aarti Industries is a capital-hungry specialty chemicals business whose ROIC (~6%) is far below my 15% floor, while net profit has collapsed from ₹1,186 Cr in FY22 to ₹331 Cr in FY25 — yet the stock trades at 43x those depressed earnings. This is precisely the kind of mediocre business that looks cheap on a normalised-earnings basis but consistently destroys the hopes of value investors waiting for a recovery.
key_strengths: Operating cash flow positive for 5/5 years, providing a baseline of real earnings
Diversified chemical portfolio (agrochemicals, pharma, dyes) limits single-end-market concentration
Revenue CAGR of 10.3% over nine years shows the business is not shrinking
key_risks: ROE 6.0% and ROCE 6.3% — both far below my 12% red-flag threshold; capital is being destroyed in real terms
Net profit fell 72% from FY22 peak (₹1,186 Cr) to FY25 (₹331 Cr) even as revenues grew — margin erosion is structural, not cyclical
Finance cost surged from ₹102 Cr to ₹275 Cr (2022–2025) while EBITDA was flat; debt service is eating equity
red_flags: ROIC ~6% — capital is not being compounded, it is being consumed
₹1,300–1,600 Cr CWIP year after year signals chronic capex inflation with no payoff yet in returns
P/E of 43x on structurally depressed earnings embeds a heroic recovery that may never arrive
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aarti had a one-year boom in FY22 (China+1 tailwind, ₹1,186 Cr net profit) that flatters the long-term record. Strip that out and the nine-year net profit CAGR is a pedestrian 2.4%. The business has been investing ₹1,300+ Cr in capex annually for the past three years and getting virtually nothing for it in return on capital — this is the hallmark of a low-moat commodity-ish chemical business, not the quality compounder the market is pricing it as.

I always ask: what would have to be true for this to be a good investment? Margins would need to nearly double from 8.8% back toward 18–20%, ROIC would need to triple, and all of this would have to happen before the 43x P/E re-rates downward. That is too many things going right simultaneously. Invert: what are the odds margins stay depressed? Given global chemical overcapacity and China re-entry, quite high. I pass.
